articles.title: Council Tables Street Tree Planting Ordinance
articles.deck: The vote came after 34 residents spoke at Wednesday’s session.
body: Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days. Residents of Lower Millrace said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street.

The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first. Councilmember Agnes Szabo asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $850.

articles.title: Letters: Orion Drive Parking Is Out of Control
body: To the editor: Please keep the seasonal farmers market in the budget. Many of us on Orion Drive use it every week.

I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the December meeting. To the editor: I have lived on Orion Drive for 26 years, and I want to say what a difference the Mill Hill Lions Club has made.
Edna Zielinski, Foundry Row

articles.deck: Residents of Foundry Row met on Friday to talk over the plan.
body: The effort began in December when a handful of neighbors met at the Bellwood Chapel to talk about after-school reading program. Organizers say the work is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Friday mornings.
The group has raised $18,500 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food.

Theodore Salazar, who has lived on Keystone Street for 31 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected. Several residents on Keystone Street said they had been waiting since 2002 for something like this.

articles.title: Zelda Zielinski, 67, Longtime Volunteer
articles.deck: Friends remember Zelda Zielinski for the many years of service to Mill Hill.
body: Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to Scout Troop 14 in his or her name. Zelda Zielinski died in July at home on Vernon Court, at the age of 67.

Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Mill Hill. Born in Mill Hill in the years after the war, Zelda Zielinski spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood.
Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to Scout Troop 14 in his or her name.
